title: Sycophancy + Deception: When Models Strategically Tell Users What They Want to Hear

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: compound failure of sycophancy + deception-by-omission is more harmful than either alone. Measuring co-occurrence and interaction directly informs risk assessment. If confirmed, prioritizes compound failures in safety evaluation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing scenarios requiring both disagreement and proactive disclosure is moderately complex. Measuring both sycophancy and omission in the same output requires two evaluation criteria. Feasible with mentor guidance but requires careful scenario construction.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Dual-failure scenario design plus measurement of two distinct failure modes in one experiment. The comparison with single-failure baselines adds a third condition. Moderate scope -- achievable in 30 hours if scenario set is kept small.

novelty.reasoning: Research on sycophancy-deception interaction exists: 'Sycophancy Is Not One Thing' (arxiv 2509.21305) shows sycophantic behaviors are causally separable with distinct internal representations. AI deception surveys (arxiv 2308.14752) document deceptive alignment and strategic behaviors. Research on sycophancy as 'social manipulation' and reward hacking through flattery is documented. However, the specific experimental design of constructing dual-failure scenarios requiring both disagreement and proactive disclosure, then measuring co-occurrence rates and interaction effects compared to single-failure baselines, has not been published. The compound failure measurement methodology is partially novel.
